Subject: Recap + next steps from today's discovery — decision criteria clarification

Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the items we agreed to clarify so you have a single-thread reference: 

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary use case: realtime underwriting assistance inside Finova's loan origination flow (token sizes ~600-1,200).
- Key decision criteria: latency (user experience), unit cost, deployment mode (data isolation requirements), and SLA guarantees.
- Stakeholder map (rough): Alex = technical champion / ML lead, Tom = economic buyer (Head of Product), Priya = procurement lead, security/legal TBD but likely in procurement loop.

Clarifications we asked for (please confirm):
1) Latency targets: is the P50/P95 target the right framing? You mentioned 150-250ms for interactive flows — please confirm P50 vs P95 expectations.
2) Cost: do you have a rough target for cost per 1K tokens or monthly run-rate budget we should optimize to?
3) Deployment preference: you indicated preference for Dedicated (VPC) but would like to know when Private (customer-managed) becomes necessary vs hosted with strong data controls.
4) SLA: what minimum uptime/response SLAs will procurement/econ buyer require to sign off?

Proposed next steps: 
- Alex: confirm the latency targets (P50 & P95) and the list of folks in security/legal who should be included.
- Priya: share procurement timeline and any vendor questionnaire we should fill out.
- Logan / Dev (cc'd): we'll follow up with a short note outlining SLA and deployment options plus a draft SOW and pricing.

Attachments: I attached the high-level security QA we usually share to speed procurement (Finova_Security_QA.pdf) and a draft SOW placeholder.

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute follow-up next week to run through numbers and procurement checklist.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@finova.com>

Date: Mon, 5 Oct 2026 09:08:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Recap + next steps from today's discovery — decision criteria clarification

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Latency: our product team measures latency at P50 and P95. Target we'd like to hit for a good UX is P50 <= 150ms and P95 <= 400ms for typical prompt sizes. For larger batch prompts in analytics, higher latency is acceptable but not for the interactive flow.

2) Cost: we don't have a firm $/1k-token goal yet, but the budget owner (Tom) has expressed concern about keeping inference spend predictable — ballpark we'd like to keep steady-state core feature spend below $20k/month but are willing to justify incremental spend for clear product impact.

3) Deployment: preference is Dedicated (VPC) to start for production due to data isolation. If Redwood Private is significantly more overhead/cost, Dedicated + strict networking controls should be acceptable. We will loop legal/security if you flag any non-standard data handling.

4) SLA: Tom will want 99.9% availability SLA for production endpoints; anything below that will need executive approval.

Stakeholders: 
- Tom Reynolds (tom.reynolds@finova.com) — economic buyer / Head of Product (please include him on procurement/contract threads).
- Priya Shah (priya.shah@finova.com) — procurement lead.
- Security: I'll confirm the security lead but will include them when we send the vendor questionnaire.

I'll loop Tom and Priya on this thread. Happy to jump on a call next Tue afternoon if that works for your team.

— Alex
Alex Turner
Head of ML, Finova

Hi Alex / Marissa —

Quick technical note on the latency/cost tradeoffs and deployment options so procurement has something tangible: 

Latency & performance
- For the interactive flow sizes you described (600-1,200 tokens), we can hit P50 ~120-160ms on a Redwood Dedicated pool configured with 2xA100-class GPUs per instance with continuous batching tuned to your traffic profile. P95 will be workload dependent but should be in the 300-450ms range; we can tighten that with higher reserved capacity.

Cost & predictability
- Dedicated (reserved capacity) gives the most predictable unit economics and is straightforward to budget monthly. If your priority is strict cost predictability under steady load, Dedicated is the recommended starting point.

Deployment modes & security
- Dedicated (VPC) supports strong network isolation and customer-managed egress rules. Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane) is available if you require on-prem or air-gapped deployments, but it comes with additional runbook overhead and license terms.

SLA options
- Standard hosted: 99.5% availability.
- Dedicated (reserved): 99.9% availability SLA (upgradeable to 99.95% with higher commitment).

I'll attach the Dedicated_capacity_pricing.pdf and SLA_options.pdf for your procurement review. Marissa — if you can share Finova's vendor questionnaire, we can start filling it out.

Thanks,
